solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Brightness of girl embracing loveless idiot

indicators.note: the girl's name holds the next piece inside it, as if hugging it

parts.note: Lucy is a girl's name

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, so the letter O is taken out of the word idiot

explanation.surface: A girl's radiance shows as she hugs a foolish man she no longer loves.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis, hence O; 'loveless' strips it to leave IDIT, which 'embracing' wraps in the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucidity is clarity or brightness, as of light or of mind; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Vulgar attire that a motorist sets off in

definitions.text: that a motorist sets off in

parts.note: low means coarse or vulgar
gear is clothing or attire

explanation.surface: A driver starts out wearing tasteless clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sets off in' looks like dressing to impress, but means pulls away.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers start moving in first, the bottom ratio of the gearbox.

clue.text: Muslim leader in American state briefly

indicators.note: the state's name is cut short to its abbreviated form

parts.note: California is a US state

explanation.surface: An Islamic ruler living in a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: Calif. is the standard short form of California.
explanation.definitionFit: A calif (caliph) was the chief civil and religious ruler of the Islamic world.

clue.text: Nasty spider in a gap — going down the plughole?

indicators.note: a nasty mess of letters: these are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A horrid spider caught in a gap, slipping away down the drain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going down the plughole is vanishing from sight, used for hopes lost too.

clue.text: Row around bend initially in river

indicators.note: the row goes around the letter taken from bend

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: only the opening letter of bend is used

explanation.surface: A rowing crew goes round a bend on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiber is the river that flows through Rome.

clue.text: Injury sending member to hospital

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
an arm is a member, or limb, of the body

explanation.surface: An injured limb means a trip to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending member to hospital' puts ARM alongside H, the hospital sign letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm is damage or hurt done to someone, a plain synonym of injury.

clue.text: Surprisingly, age is no worry

indicators.note: the letters arrive in a surprising order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A reassurance that getting older is nothing to fret about.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise over something is to worry about it intensely.

clue.text: Meat chopped up and cold, in pit

indicators.note: the cold letter goes inside the pit

parts.note: a pit is a mine, as a coal pit
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Meat cut up and kept cold down a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Mince is meat finely chopped or ground.

clue.text: Sporting characters? Many are in suits

parts.note: playing means taking part in sport
a card is a character, an eccentric person

explanation.surface: Sporty types who often dress in suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suits' suggests business wear but means hearts, clubs, diamonds and spades.
explanation.definitionFit: A pack is divided into four suits, so its cards are in suits.

clue.text: Sound of large mammals in the country

indicators.note: the clue asks for the sound of a word, so a word said aloud gives a different spelling

parts.note: whales are the largest mammals

explanation.surface: Whale song heard somewhere in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Wales is one of the countries of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Dance with nothing on? That's swell!

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Going to a dance wearing nothing is greeted with a cheery 'swell!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' looks like an exclamation of approval but is the verb: to swell up.
explanation.definitionFit: To balloon is to expand or puff up, which is what swelling means.

clue.text: Little mischief selfish? Not entirely

indicators.note: only part of the word selfish is used, so the answer lies inside it

explanation.surface: Asks whether a naughty child is being selfish, or only a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischief can mean a mischievous person; a small sprite who plays tricks fits that exactly.

clue.text: Shared communication system — a political policy?

definitions.meaning: a telephone line shared by several subscribers
the official line a political party takes

explanation.surface: A shared phone line doubles as a party's agreed position.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a shared telephone connection and a party's official stance.

clue.text: Possible wearer of leather jacket in this chair?

definitions.meaning: a member of the 1960s British biker subculture known for leather jackets
a chair on curved runners that tilts back and forth

explanation.surface: Pictures a biker in leathers sitting in a particular chair.
explanation.walkthrough: Rockers were 1960s British motorcycle enthusiasts, rivals of the Mods.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the leather-clad biker and a chair that tips to and fro.

clue.text: Restraint of one opposing monster endlessly

parts.note: con is the opposing side, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: the last letter of the monster is dropped

parts.note: a troll is a monster of folklore

explanation.surface: Holding back from opposing an unending monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-control is restraint; the noun means holding something in check.

clue.text: Messengers set to put in half of answer

indicators.note: the word for set is placed inside the other piece
only the first three of the six letters of answer are used

parts.note: to gel is to set, as jelly does

explanation.surface: Instructions to slot a word into part of an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'answer' looks like a reference to the solution itself, but it is just a six-letter word to be halved by 'half of'; 'to put in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek the word for angel means messenger; angels bring word from God.

clue.text: Dog for breaking up demo, say

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A dog is used to break up a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Samoyed is a white Siberian breed of dog.

clue.text: Wide-ranging alarm when old male beast is trapped

indicators.note: the old male beast is caught inside the word for alarm

parts.note: panic is sudden alarm
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Alarm spreads widely when an old ram gets caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoramic view takes in a broad sweep, so it is wide in range.

clue.text: Publication offers worthless writing with little hesitation

parts.note: pap is trivial, worthless reading matter
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A newspaper serving up worthless prose with a bit of dithering.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper is a newspaper or journal, a publication.

clue.text: Woman, one crushed by horse

indicators.note: the one is squeezed inside the horse

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A woman is crushed by a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie is a woman's name, an example of the class.

clue.text: Not a word from this parent?

definitions.text: Not a word from this parent?

parts.words: Not a word from this parent?
parts.note: the word means both keeping silent and a mother, so a silent mother fits

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an informal British name for a mother and also means saying nothing.

clue.text: 19 across's half-hearted affair

indicators.note: one of the two letters at the heart of the word is dropped

parts.note: a matter is an affair or business

explanation.surface: A mother's lukewarm love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: MATTER has a double T at its heart; losing one leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mater is Latin for mother, used in old-fashioned British slang for one's mum.

clue.text: Associate seen as 'catch' on reflection, right?

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to entrap is to catch

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a colleague is really a good catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' suggests a romantic prize but is the verb; 'on reflection' reads its synonym backwards as PARTNE.
explanation.definitionFit: A business associate or companion is a partner; a straight synonym.

clue.text: Toad's friend is irritable

definitions.meaning: in The Wind in the Willows, Toad's friend the Water Rat is nicknamed this

explanation.surface: Toad's companion is in a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wind in the Willows is a classic English children's book with Toad, Mole, Badger and the Water Rat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the nickname of the Water Rat in the book, and a British word for grumpy.

clue.text: Part to go round audibly

indicators.note: the word is heard, not seen, so a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: to roll is to go round, turning over

explanation.surface: An actor's part involves going round in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's role is the part they play.

clue.text: Having lots of free time and terribly idle, certain to be hiding

indicators.note: the rearranged letters conceal the word for certain inside them
the letters of idle are badly mixed up

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone with time on their hands is surely terribly idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' gives LEID, and 'to be hiding' means that jumble holds the word for certain.
explanation.definitionFit: The leisured classes are those with ample free time; synonym.
